title: fix(scripts): tell the root-reaching sweeps to skip `.objectui-tmp`
body:
Fixes #9201

`check:i18n-dead-keys` runs a whole-tree filesystem `grep -rFn` whose skip set did
not name `.objectui-tmp`. That directory is not clutter — it is **live**:
`withGeneratedApp()` in `packages/cli/src/__tests__/app-generator.test.ts` mkdtemps
a generated app under `REPO_ROOT/.objectui-tmp/` and removes it in a `finally`, inside
the same shard the gate runs in. The sweep descends into a scratch tree that is
being torn down underneath it, and the gate **dies**.

⛔ Not a flake, and it must never be closed as one. What varies is the
interleaving; the outcome once the two overlap does not. ⛔ The fix is never a
retry, never a wider catch, never swallowing exit 2.

## The exit-2 control flow — triage's claim, verified here, not inherited

Verified twice, both empirically, on this branch's tree:

```
$ grep -rFn -I -e 'objectui9201.probe.marker' -- .objectui-tmp/probe-9201 /nonexistent/vanished.ts
.objectui-tmp/probe-9201/marker.ts:2:export const probe = t('objectui9201.probe.marker');
grep: /nonexistent/vanished.ts: No such file or directory
grep exit=2   <-- 2, despite a match   (grep (GNU grep) 3.11)
```

```
$ node -e "…textFootprint('A_ROOT_THAT_DOES_NOT_EXIST', [KEY])…"
THREW from the gate catch block
  error.status  = 2
  error.stderr  = grep: …: No such file or directory
```

⇒ GNU grep answers a file error with exit **2 even on a run that also matched**,
and `textFootprint()`'s catch absorbs **only** `error.status === 1` (no match) and
re-throws everything else. So the vanishing scratch file does not produce a log
line — it produces an uncaught throw, and the shard goes red for a reason that has
nothing to do with the code under test. **Triage's claim is confirmed as written.**

That catch is correct and is now pinned: an absorbed IO error returns an empty
footprint, and an empty footprint reads as "this key is dead" — the most confident
possible rendering of a broken tool.

## Re-located coordinates

objectui#8754 round 1 landed on `check-i18n-dead-keys.mjs` earlier the same day
(`collectIndirectTemplateHeads()` is present in the file), so every line number in
the card and in triage's comment was re-located **by content** before it was used:

| cited | actually at (this branch's base `4c0dc090a1`) |
|:--|:--|
| `check-i18n-dead-keys.mjs:428-431` (`TEXT_SWEEP_SKIP_DIRS`) | **:461-464** |
| `check-i18n-dead-keys.mjs:606-612` (sweep argv) | **:635-643** |
| `check-i18n-dead-keys.mjs:616` (`execFileSync` + catch) | **:646-659** |
| `check-comment-mask-corpus.mjs:246` (the lit convention control) | **:246** — unmoved; header reason at **:230-243** |
| `.gitignore:50` | **:50** — unmoved |
| `app-generator.test.ts:1386-1396` (`withGeneratedApp`) | **:1382-1396** |

One coordinate the card did not have: this file runs the skip set through **two**
sweeps, `textFootprint()` and `derivePackObjectImporters()`. The second is
subtree-scoped (`IMPORTER_SEARCH_DIRS = packages apps examples e2e`) and cannot
reach the root, so it was never at risk — it simply shares the constant.

## ① The change

`TEXT_SWEEP_SKIP_DIRS` gains `.objectui-tmp`, with the reasoning written down next
to it. `scripts/check-comment-mask-corpus.mjs`, the sibling whole-tree sweep, has
excluded it on exactly this reasoning all along (`SKIPPED_DIRECTORIES`, and its
header states the reason) — this was the one of the two that had not been told.

## ② The 12 candidates, classified — all 12, with a reason

Triage's population was selected by one spelling of the skip mechanism and is
explicitly **"candidates to classify", not "12 defects"**. The question asked of
each: **does it actually scan the repo ROOT?**

| # | script | reaches the repo root? | verdict |
|--:|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | `body-dialect-census.mjs` | **YES** — walks `--root` (default `.`) and descends dot-directories | **exclusion added** |
| 2 | `check-i18n-call-site-keys.mjs` | no — `collectSourceFiles()` walks only `['packages','apps']`, and its walk also skips every `entry.name.startsWith('.')` | no exclusion needed |
| 3 | `check-i18n-dead-keys.mjs` | **YES** — `grep -rFn … -- root` | **exclusion added (the card)** |
| 4 | `check-lint-rule-coverage.mjs` | **YES** — `descend(root)` | **no hardcoded exclusion, deliberately** — see below |
| 5 | `check-lucide-icon-record-names.mjs` | no — `SCAN_ROOTS = ['packages','apps','examples']` | no exclusion needed |
| 6 | `check-node-esm-load.mjs` | no — `emittedSources(srcDir)` per discovered package; never above `PKG/src` | no exclusion needed |
| 7 | `check-phantom-dependencies.mjs` | no — `PACKAGE_ROOTS = ['packages','apps']`; `listSourceFiles()` also skips all dot-entries | no exclusion needed |
| 8 | `check-type-check-coverage.mjs` | no — `GROUPS = ['packages','apps','examples']`; walk skips all dot-entries | no exclusion needed |
| 9 | `check-unreferenced-sources.mjs` | no — `PACKAGE_ROOTS = ['packages','apps']`; shares phantom-deps' dot-skipping walk | no exclusion needed |
| 10 | `check-unused-dependencies.mjs` | no — `listPackageFiles(pkgDir)` per `discoverPackages()` entry; skips all dot-entries | no exclusion needed |
| 11 | `markdown-test-inputs.mjs` | no — `SCAN_ROOTS = ['packages','apps','examples','eslint-rules','scripts']` | no exclusion needed |
| 12 | `unit-registry-collision.mjs` | no — `collectFiles()` starts at `root/DIR` taken from the `unit` project's include globs (`packages/**`, `examples/**`, `eslint-rules/**`, `scripts/**`) | no exclusion needed |

⛔ Nothing was silently skipped: 12 of 12 carry a verdict and a reason.

**#1 `body-dialect-census.mjs` was measured, not read.** Planting the same bytes
twice and running the census through its own exported `census()`:

```
BEFORE — census hit LINES under .objectui-tmp/:
  .objectui-tmp/probe-9201/census-probe.md:38  type=button  body=false
  .objectui-tmp/probe-9201/census-probe.md:33  type=page    body=true
BEFORE — lit control under probe-9201-control/:
  probe-9201-control/census-probe.md:38  type=button  body=false
  probe-9201-control/census-probe.md:33  type=page    body=true

AFTER  — .objectui-tmp/ hits:  (none)  <-- excluded
AFTER  — lit control hits:     probe-9201-control/census-probe.md:38, :33
```

So it was reporting tooling scratch as corpus. Same class as the `test-results`
and `playwright-report` entries its skip list already carried. Exclusion added.

**#4 `check-lint-rule-coverage.mjs` reaches the root but must NOT get a hardcoded
entry, and that is a reasoned verdict rather than an omission.** Its
`STRUCTURAL_SKIP_DIRS` is contractually two entries — its own header says both are
"structural rather than lint policy" and that "every OTHER pruned directory is
derived from the live config". The gate measures *what `eslint .` actually walks*;
pruning a directory ESLint does not prune would make the gate lie about the
population it exists to report. And it is already handled, by a derived mechanism,
measured through the gate's own `gitIgnoreReading()`:

```
derived git-ignore filter (the mechanism that prunes this gate's census):
  IGNORED -> dropped from census  .objectui-tmp/probe-9201/marker.ts
  visible -> stays in census      probe-9201-control/marker.ts
  visible -> stays in census      packages/react/src/index.ts
  controls: controlIgnored=true controlVisible=true
```

It is also structurally immune to the race that motivates this card: it reads no
file *contents* during the walk (`readdirSync` inside `try/catch`,
`eslint.isPathIgnored()` and `git check-ignore` are both path-only), so a file
vanishing mid-walk cannot throw.

⚠️ Triage's own boundary, carried: the 12 are **not the complete set** — the one
script that already excluded `.objectui-tmp`, `check-comment-mask-corpus.mjs`,
is itself absent from them, having spelled its skip set a different way. The
root-reaching population is therefore **4**, not 12: the three above plus
`check-comment-mask-corpus.mjs`, which already complied.

## ③ Position on unifying the two skip sets: do not unify, and do not file a card yet

Triage ruled unification out of this card and asked for a position, conditioned on
duplication being *confirmed* after ②. **It is not confirmed — measured, the sets
are not duplicates.** The three root-reaching hardcoded sets, after this PR:

```
sizes: comment-mask-corpus=12   i18n-dead-keys=9   body-dialect-census=12
common core (8): .git .next .objectui-tmp .turbo build coverage dist node_modules

comment-mask-corpus   unique to it: .playwright-mcp .source
i18n-dead-keys        unique to it: .changeset
body-dialect-census   unique to it: .pnpm-store out
```

Every one of the three carries at least one entry the other two deliberately lack,
and `.changeset` is the sharp one: a changeset that *mentions* an i18n key is not a
reference to it, so the dead-key sweep must not read that tree — while the census,
whose corpus is exactly authored metadata examples, gets real hits from
`.changeset/` and must keep reading it. A shared constant would have to either drop
`.changeset` (reintroducing false liveness into the dead-key gate) or impose it
(blinding the census to a population it is measuring). The common core is 8 of
9-to-12 entries; the residue is where the meaning is.

⇒ My position: **do not unify, and no new card.** Triage's reasoning ("unifying now
would copy a wrong set onto the one correct one") holds for a second reason after
②: the sets are not wrong, they are *different on purpose*. The right shared thing
would be a named "tooling-written, holds no source" subset that each gate composes
with its own semantics — worth doing only if a fourth root-reaching sweep appears
and misses it again. Filing a card for that today would be filing a card for an
abstraction nothing is yet asking for.

## ⛔ Acceptance — the two-sided probe, both legs, matched lines

The same bytes planted twice, run through the gate's own `textFootprint()`:

```
BEFORE the fix
  gate hit files for objectui9201.probe.marker:
    .objectui-tmp/probe-9201/marker.ts:2:export const probe = t('objectui9201.probe.marker');
    probe-9201-control/marker.ts:2:export const probe = t('objectui9201.probe.marker');
  LEG A  .objectui-tmp/ ............ PRESENT in gate output
  LEG B  probe-9201-control/ (lit) . PRESENT in gate output

AFTER the fix
  gate hit files for objectui9201.probe.marker:
    probe-9201-control/marker.ts:2:export const probe = t('objectui9201.probe.marker');
  LEG A  .objectui-tmp/ ............ ABSENT from gate output
  LEG B  probe-9201-control/ (lit) . PRESENT in gate output

  (the excluded leg is still on disk and still matches:)
  .objectui-tmp/probe-9201/marker.ts:2:export const probe = t('objectui9201.probe.marker');
```

⭐ The lit leg is not decoration. Without it, "absent from the output" is
indistinguishable from a sweep that found nothing at all.

⚠️ `.objectui-tmp` is `.gitignore`d (`git check-ignore -v` → `.gitignore:50`), which
is why every `git grep`-based tool in this tree is blind to it and only a filesystem
sweep ever hit it. The fixture is therefore a real on-disk, untracked path — that is
what makes it a valid stand-in for the CLI test's scratch tree.

**Live control.** The real gate was then run with a scratch tree present on disk:
`pnpm check:i18n-dead-keys` → exit **0**, and `grep -c 'objectui9201\|objectui-tmp'`
over its full output → **0**. The directory existed, the gate neither crashed nor
reported it.

## Tests

Both changes are pinned two-sided, and the exit-2 posture is pinned so nobody can
make a future red shard green by widening the catch:

- `scripts/__tests__/check-i18n-dead-keys.test.ts` — planted-hit exclusion with its
  lit control; plus `status === 2` + `stderr` envelope on the re-throw.
- `scripts/__tests__/body-dialect-census.test.ts` — the same two-sided shape for `census()`.

**Ablation** (fix committed first, mutation proven on disk by blob hash, restored by
`git checkout HEAD -- PATH` and verified byte-identical):

```
HEAD blobs:     A=30e30037c7… B=aac415fe65…
mutated blobs:  A=83c9483539… B=fad86b46fa…   (both differ => the mutation reached disk)
MUTATED RUN     vitest exit=1
  × skips a planted hit under `.objectui-tmp/` while the SAME bytes elsewhere are found
  × finds a planted node in a scanned directory and NOT the same bytes under `.objectui-tmp/`
  Test Files 2 failed (2) | Tests 2 failed | 136 passed (138)
restored blobs: A=30e30037c7… B=aac415fe65…   (identical to HEAD; git diff HEAD empty)
```

Only the two new pins turn red; the 136 others — the lit legs included — stay green,
so the failure is the missing exclusion and not a broken walk.

## Gates run locally (exit codes captured before any pipe)

| command | exit |
|:--|--:|
| `pnpm exec vitest run --project unit` (the two edited suites, 138 tests) | **0** |
| `pnpm check:i18n-dead-keys` (under the shared verify lock; `VERDICT command-exit 0`) | **0** |
| `pnpm check:control-bytes` | **0** |
| `pnpm check:comment-mask-corpus` | **0** |
| `pnpm check:changeset-claims` | **0** |
| `pnpm check:new-line-citations` | **0** |
| `pnpm type-check:scripts` | **0** |
| `pnpm lint:root` | **0** (0 errors, 32 pre-existing warnings) |

`type-check:scripts` is a measurement, not a claim: `tsc -p tsconfig.scripts.json
--listFiles` lists **both** edited test files in its program. Repo-wide scans
(`turbo run lint`, the full shard matrix) are CI's.

Changeset: `.changeset/9201-sweep-skip-objectui-tmp.md`, **empty frontmatter** — this
diff is `scripts/` + its tests and publishes nothing. Added as a new file (`git status`
showed `??`, never `M`).

`node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test THE_5_PATHS` → **NOT GOVERNED**.
Left as a **draft** regardless; the PM seat lands it.
